summary: Created from the MPI-467 smoke fill running out of space at model 9 of 12 on a 350 GB volume the preflight had passed.

MECHANISM CORRECTED on this card - I had written 'aria2 preallocates its .part files', which is WRONG, and it reintroduced a mislabel the codebase had already fixed. wrapper.py:1754 states it plainly: aria2 writes -s 128 segments at scattered offsets with --file-allocation=none, so the .part file is SPARSE - its logical size snaps to ~the full total the moment a late segment writes near EOF, while allocated blocks are only what arrived. The same comment records this being 'mislabeled an aria2 preallocation artifact in MPI-95; there is no preallocation here'. The finding and the fix are unchanged and the severity goes UP: the gate's error is near worst-case rather than proportional, because an in-flight 21 GB weight reads as ~21 GB used within minutes of starting. Independent confirmation arrived from RunPod's own console at the same time - its telemetry showed 269 GB while the wrapper reported 288.8 GB on the identical volume.

summary: Bug 1: du -sb summed apparent bytes; the comment above it claimed the opposite, which is why two rewrites of the route missed it. Fixed at BOTH du call sites, wrapper 0.2.44. Bug 2: new pure volumeFitVerdict gate runs after the download Pod is up and before the first install - the earliest moment free space is knowable - and refuses to rent when measured free cannot take the remainder. 7 asserts with a negative control. Correction recorded: the gate first reused VOLUME_HEADROOM_GB (40GB) as a required free margin and would have refused a from-empty fill that genuinely fits; separate FIT_MARGIN_GB=5 now. Also recorded: with honest numbers this gate would NOT have stopped 2026-08-08 - that was bug 1.

summary: Release note written. docs/releases/UNRELEASED.md gained a fixes bullet for bug 1 - the remote disk-full pre-flight shipped in v1.3.1 (8763ef81), so the inflated free-space number is reachable by real users, not a dev-only defect. Bullet describes the symptom in user terms (a part-finished download counted at its full final size, an install refused with 39GB free while ~91GB was, and a free-up-space message that was not the remedy). npm run release:check passes.

Live Pod session: wrapper 0.2.44 PUBLISHED to dev and verified booting on six CPU Pods (wrapperVersion 0.2.44), so mpi-release's manifest-diff stop will now read dev 0.2.44 vs stable 0.2.40 and the answer is still PROMOTE. The disk measurement itself is INCONCLUSIVE and the card stays open: two runs of the same experiment disagreed - at 14.1s a 14.31GB .part was attributed 13.61GB of volume (95% of declared, reads as apparent) while at 7.6s the same experiment attributed 0.00GB. Root problem is that /remote/pod/disk cannot answer the question: /wrapper/disk caches du for 60s and is invalidated only by an install completing or a delete, the app's downloadedBytes lags the wrapper by seconds which is gigabytes at 250-460MB/s, and R2 is fast enough that a download finishes before a Pod delete lands (a 2.15GB dep hit 99.96%; a 14.31GB one went 29% -> 98% AFTER delete-active returned deleted:true). The right instrument already exists: GET /wrapper/ls returns allocated blocks in top_level and apparent bytes in models_files for the SAME file at the SAME instant, and its own comment says the totals differ while a sparse .part is present. No app route surfaces it and direct egress to the pod proxy fails from this machine (curl 000), so the next step is a small app route proxying /wrapper/ls. Also found: an in-flight huggingface install does not touch the volume at all (49,664 bytes used with 1.27GB fetched, jumping to 26.37GB on completion), which may undercut the card's premise that a partial inflates du - resolve that before calling the fix right. Full-disk phrase stays OUT of the release note.

Built the instrument this card was missing, at Fabio's go-ahead: GET /remote/pod/ls in routes/remotePodLifecycle.js, a read-only passthrough of the wrapper's /wrapper/ls plus a pure compareVolumeAccounting() returning blockBytes (du -s --block-size=1 for the dir holding MODELS_DIR), apparentBytes (sum of os.path.getsize), and phantomBytes = apparent - blocks, which is exactly what the pre-fix du -sb would have invented. Both halves come from ONE response at ONE instant, removing the race that made the live session inconclusive. countedDir/approximate are reported because models_files walks MODELS_DIR while blocks come per top-level dir. Next attempt is one request during a big aria2 install: a large positive phantomBytes means the bug is real and the fix removes it; near zero means RunPod volumes allocate the full length and the card's premise does not hold. tests/volume-accounting-gap.test.cjs, 6 cases, mutation-checked - the sibling-prefix case is a proven negative control, and it only became one after the mutation exposed that the first version was written with the prefix backwards and guarded nothing. files.json updated to own routes/remotePodLifecycle.js and the new test.

MEASURED IN ONE REQUEST, and bug 1's premise DOES NOT HOLD. GET /remote/pod/ls sampled every 1.5s through a 14.31GB aria2/R2 install on a throwaway 40GB volume: phantomBytes never left +/-15MB on a 14.31GB file (0.1%). 2.4s in, with 50MB fetched, the .part was already 13.43GB apparent AND 13.43GB of allocated blocks - a RunPod network volume charges the full declared length immediately, so du -sb and du -s --block-size=1 agree and the shipped flag swap changes nothing measurable. It stays as the correct accounting for a quota (the old comment asserted the opposite of what the flag did), but it must NOT be described as the fix for a 48.65GB over-count. That gap is explained by the two numbers not being taken at the same instant: at 250-460 MB/s a console figure 2-3 minutes stale is 48GB behind by arithmetic, which is exactly what this instrument was built to eliminate. Last session's contradictory legs both resolve - leg H is today's behaviour, leg I was /remote/pod/disk's 60s du cache answering with the pre-install number. Bug 2 (the smoke preflight free-space gate) is untouched and stays. Two corrections fell out: docs/download-manager.md's 'the HF path stages OFF the volume' section was wrong (HF stages into <dest>.part.hfstage INSIDE MODELS_DIR by design) and is replaced, and a killed install strands that staging tree - neither the wrapper delete nor the app uninstall removes it, and the disk gate then counts a dep's own stranded .part against its retry.
